body:
Builds one handler-coverage command (v030-07): after a set of kept recorded checks (check-{n}.json, Check::from_bytes then Check::replay) has run on the stand, it lists exactly the UI graph's handlers, a graph node's id and a handler's event name as DioxusDocument::graph reads them, that none of those checks exercised.
States the canvas limit in the acceptance: only DOM listeners on agent-visible nodes are counted, one per (node, event); handlers a canvas dispatches inside one listener are not, the command keyed on the graph node id with its optional owner, never on a NodeId, so 0.4.0 can extend it.
Adds the owed replay test (CARRY cry-sxrivdk3): a session holding an actions step is recorded, kept as a check, read back and replayed on a fresh session of the same app, the replay holding with an equal actions answer, and a differing answer naming the step and the differing key; v030-06 reads verified once it passes.
The coverage read is read-only over the screen; the UI graph, the snapshot, the stable-id grammar and the actions verb keep their shapes and are only read.

The read-only UI graph (DioxusDocument::graph): one node per snapshot node, names and closed words only, never a second role or name mapping; the coverage command reads its nodes' handlers and must add no mapping of its own.

The listener rule behind the graph's handlers: the vdom walk's exact current listeners, an event other than mounted, so a listener a re-render removed is not counted; the data-dioxus-id mark serves event dispatch alone and is not the coverage key.

The actionable-key rule and author_id: every actionable element reads a stable author key carried as its AccessKit author_id; the coverage list keys handlers on that stable graph id (with its optional owner), never on an engine NodeId.

DioxusDocument::actionable_nodes and the actions verb: the owed replay test records and replays a kept actions step, its answer compared key by key against the kept one, the actionable rule unchanged.

The snapshot model the replay reads (role, name, focus and states from accessibility_tree; enabled, value, checked and clickable from the element and the vdom walk): the replayed actions answer must equal the kept one under that model.

Redaction of what the coverage result carries: no control value, typed text or page text beyond ids, component and event names; a password input's MASKED_VALUE and a file input's marker never leave as text through a new result field.
The driver's disabled refusal: a click or type is refused as disabled where the snapshot's enabled reads Some(false), nothing dispatched; a replayed step refused that way reached no handler.
The canvas limit as a boundary of the count: handlers dispatched inside one canvas listener are not counted; virtual nodes are 0.4.0's, no canvas renderer or virtual-node production in this chunk.

a new log line or span from escher's own targets passes the obs allowlist, text, value, html and attrs redacted, ids and closed words only

Motion, focus ring, colour scheme and user-preference rules; the chunk paints nothing.

body: **2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the one actionable rule and the check's listener leg) — retired `unkeyed_actionable`'s reading of the `data-dioxus-id` mark. Both `unkeyed_actionable` and `actionable_nodes` now read one crate-private rule, `Readings`, whose listener leg is the vdom walk's exact current listeners other than `mounted`. A listener removed on a re-render is read by neither, and a unit test witnesses that the mark outlives it. This chunk's handler set must follow the same listener leg and must not read the mark or add a second rule.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the actionable-node reader) — added `DioxusDocument::actionable_nodes`, an `ActionableNode` of `id`, `owner` and `keyed`, under the `accessibility` feature in the `actionable` module. It lists nodes in snapshot pre-order, and its domain is the UI graph's nodes, so an inert or hidden element is not listed. This is the agreement check the coverage handler set rests on, and it sets the hidden-node boundary of the count.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the keyed reading, provisional on the carriers) — the `keyed` field on the `actions` answer is PROVISIONAL until the founder's own word. The owed replay test compares `actions` answers key by key, so it reads `keyed` while the field is still provisional. The test must not settle that status.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the actions verb as a read-only reader) — `Session::actions` answers each instance verb with the cause `check_target` would give. It changes nothing and writes ids, owner ids, verb and cause words and booleans only, never a value, `MASKED_VALUE` or `NodeId`. On the stand the flight booker's options read `covered` with owner `flight-type`, `flight-return-date` reads `disabled` and `crud-person-14` reads `off-screen`. This is the answer the owed replay test keeps and re-asserts, and the redaction model the coverage output must match.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the actionable counts at boot and the Cells answer's bound) — `ACTIONABLE_AT_BOOT` pins Counter 2, Flight Booker 7, Timer 3, CRUD 11, Cells 678 and the load page 2. On Cells the unpaged `actions` answer is 106,088 bytes, a stated limit owned by residual `res-7cc5bi4k`. These are the per-task counts a coverage handler set can be checked against. A Cells-wide unexercised list meets the same size bound.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the read-only UI graph reader DioxusDocument::graph) — introduced `UiGraph`, which holds one `GraphNode` per snapshot node: its id, `owner`, component, handlers with their declared writes, and the states it reads. The graph carries names and closed words only, is gated by `accessibility` (the `signal_registry` module is not gated), and adds no second role or name mapping. `stand_graph` asserts that no served id holds the reserved `///`. This chunk lists its handlers (`GraphNode.handlers`, `GraphHandler.event`) and must keep this shape and this redaction.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (graph state registration and the bridge dispatch's write record) — `use_graph_state`/`DeclaredWrite` and the `SignalRegistry` record dispatches only where an app registered state. A page with no registered state reaches no registry. This is the scope's P3 premise: no "exercised" reader holds on every app. Any new exercised record must leave this registry behaviour and the `confirmed`/`unconfirmed` reading unchanged.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the «reacts to a click» snapshot field built as NodeState.clickable) — `clickable` is read from the vdom walk's current `click` listeners on an element that is no disabled form control. `NODE_FIELDS` went from 13 to 14 and `Reading::ALL` from 11 to 12. The `CLICKABLE` table reads Cells 676 and Circle Drawer 1, against the listener mark's 677. A coverage count of click handlers must not contradict this reading. The chunk must also add no node key, so `NODE_FIELDS` stays at fourteen.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** (the «reacts to a click» reading measured by link 2) — measured the stand's (node, event) listeners: Cells' 676 cells take `click` and `cells-grid` takes `keydown`, `counter-increment` takes `click`, and `crud-list` takes `keydown`. These are the handlers an exact unexercised list on the stand must name, keydown handlers included.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** (the listener mark's over-report and the actionable-key check) — a listener removed on a re-render leaves its event attribute and the `data-dioxus-id` mark standing, and a `mounted` listener writes none. Only the vdom walk's dynamic attributes read current listeners exactly. This is a trap for this chunk: a handler record read from the mark or the attributes over-reports.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** (the probe target outside the a11y leg) — `dioxus_runtime_probe` runs in the workspace `test` leg only, outside the `a11y` and `stand-repeat` legs. It witnesses the listener reading that the graph's handlers take. This is the precedent for placing a new test file outside the a11y leg's fourteen files.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — established the founder's actionable-key rule: every focusable, interactive-role or listener-bearing element reads an author key carried as its `author_id`. `unkeyed_actionable` is the check for that rule. Trap: never satisfy the check with a `tabindex` or a role, because that moves the pinned Tab order; key the element instead. The coverage output keys on these author keys.

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — every element node of a Dioxus document carries its stable id as AccessKit `author_id`, and no `TextRun`, document-root or `Window` node carries one. This is the key the coverage list must use instead of a `NodeId`.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — established the snapshot as a consumer of the accessibility tree that must never re-derive role or name ("no second role or name mapping"). The graph and any coverage read inherit this ban.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — a password input reads `MASKED_VALUE` and the snapshot reads `enabled` from the presence of `disabled`. The coverage result must carry no control value or typed text, so a masked value never leaves through it.
**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — extended the value mask to a file input with a non-empty `value`. This is the second marker the coverage output must never carry as text.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — the obs sink prints only safe fields for engine targets and redacts `text`, `value`, `html` and `attrs` for `escher_*` targets. Any coverage or replay-failure log line must keep to the same redaction.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `escher-driver` names `accessibility` on `dioxus-native-dom` unconditionally, with no `[features]` table, and seven_guis gets the feature through that edge. A coverage command in the driver reads the gated `graph` through this edge, adding no feature table.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — `Session::run` refuses a `click` or `type` as `disabled` when the snapshot's `enabled` is `Some(false)`, with nothing dispatched. A replayed step refused this way reaches no handler, so it must not count as exercising one.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** (Enter and Space activate a focused control) — a pressed Enter or a released Space dispatches a synthesized Click, so the app's `onclick` runs, then `handle_click`. A recorded keyboard check therefore exercises click handlers, and the exercised record must catch that dispatch, not pointer clicks alone.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** (`disabled` by presence, the CRUD list's keys and the keyboard check) — `crud-list` takes `tabindex="0"` and an `onkeydown` (Arrow, Home and End), and `stand_keyboard` became the keyboard check. `crud-list`'s keydown is a (node, event) handler that counts as exercised only where a check pressed a key on it. Disabled-ness was keyed by presence.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** (§5, §6: `inert` and `disabled` in focus order, keys and the hit) — disabled-ness for the pointer, click, activation and focus gates is read by `ElementData::is_disabled`, meaning presence on a form control. A truthy `inert` removes focusability, hits and the tree node. Steps stopped by these gates reach no handler, and inert subtrees fall outside the graph's node set.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (`optgroup`, its role, its name and its options) — `display: none` excludes a node except an option under a select (`is_select_option`), and `hidden`, `inert` and `visibility: hidden` still exclude it. This hidden-content rule bounds which handlers are on graph nodes and therefore which are counted.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (Cells by keyboard) — `cells-grid` gained `onkeydown`, which moved the reacting-element count from 676 to 677. This count is a precedent that measurement disproved a forecast. It is also the source of the keydown handler on the Cells grid that the coverage list counts.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** (the flight booker's select in the stand's tables and readings) — a driver `click` on a flight-type option is refused `covered`. That replayed step dispatches nothing, so the option's handlers are not exercised by it.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** (the served pages, their open gap, the lint's option overlap and the scrollbar's band) — right after a `scroll`, a pointerdown in the shown overlay scrollbar band is a thumb drag and dispatches nothing. A swallowed click leaves its target's handlers unexercised. The record must key on the dispatches that happened, never on the steps issued.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (an open list against `:open`, clips and `opacity`) — a driver `click` on an element under an open select list is refused `covered`. This is another refused step that must read as exercising nothing.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (what the snapshot and an assistive technology read of an open list) — there is no `expanded` node key, and `NODE_FIELDS` was then 13 (now 14). This is the precedent that the snapshot keeps its shape and a new reading lands elsewhere. This chunk adds no node key.

**2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep** (every stand task keyed; the click-without-role count) — `unkeyed_actionable` reads 0 on every stand task, and the elements that react to a click with no role are pinned (Circle Drawer 1, Cells 676). The coverage handler set can be checked for agreement against this all-keyed baseline.

**2026-10-24-a11y-re-read** — the `a11y` leg runs fourteen files on the founder's word. Whether a new coverage or replay test file joins that leg is the founder's or §9's call, not this chunk's default.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the `a11y` leg's counts and the `stand-repeat` list) — the a11y leg reads 14 files and 114 tests, and `stand-repeat` names seventeen `--test` words. These are the tallies the chunk must keep green or move explicitly if a new test joins a leg.

**2026-10-26-codebase-health** — the `stand-repeat` list's membership is held jointly by `stand_requirement_sweep`'s leg check and `test_stand_repeat_leg_runs_three_rounds`. A new `stand_*` file joins `stand-repeat` by its prefix. Trap: a name dropped from one site alone is not detected.

partial — the chunk adds no UI surface, role, focus path, key binding or painted state; it reads the UI graph, whose node set, keys and handler reading the a11y plan's screen-reader section governs (§7 Screen Reader Support: snapshot model, actionable-key rule, author_id).

- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (snapshot model) requires the read-only UI graph (`DioxusDocument::graph`) to hold one node per snapshot node, names and closed words only, never a second role or name mapping; the coverage command reads that graph and must not derive its own node set or role/name mapping.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (actionable-key rule) requires every actionable element to read an author key carried as its AccessKit `author_id`, stable under edits of surrounding code; the coverage output keyed on the graph's node id (and optional `owner`), never on a `NodeId`, must hold to that key.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (actionable-key rule) requires `unkeyed_actionable` and `actionable_nodes` to read one actionable rule whose listener leg is the vdom walk's exact current listeners holding an event other than `mounted`, the `data-dioxus-id` mark serving event dispatch alone; whether the graph's `GraphNode.handlers` already reads that same leg (and so whether `mounted` is excluded from the handler count and a re-render-removed listener uncounted) is research's question.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (snapshot model) requires `clickable` to be read from the vdom walk's current `click` listeners on an element that is no disabled form control, not from the listener mark; a coverage count of click handlers should not contradict that reading.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (password masking) requires a password input's typed text to appear in no snapshot field or tree node (`MASKED_VALUE`); the coverage read carries no control value or typed text, consistent with the scope's read-only boundary.
- a11y-plan §6 Visual Design Verification (visibility and hit-testing) requires nodes under `display: none`, `visibility: hidden` or `inert` to be absent from the tree and so from the snapshot; handlers on such nodes are therefore outside the graph's node set — whether the command reports them as unexercised or not at all is research's question.

- §7 Screen Reader Support: `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` as the single actionable-rule check, returning nothing on every stand task — the coverage command's handler set can be checked against `actionable_nodes` for agreement on the stand.
- §3 A11y Assertion Harness Contract: headless assertions over the built tree in both layout modes, each a stated table with its row count asserted — the form the owed `actions` replay test and the coverage test can follow.
- §5 Keyboard Navigation (test harness pattern): `stand_keyboard` drives Enter / Space through the harness's `press` / `press_with`; a recorded check exercising a handler by keyboard rather than click is a candidate row for the "exercised" set.

- A second role, name or actionable mapping beside the graph/snapshot model (banned by §7 Screen Reader Support: "never a second role or name mapping").
- Keying coverage output on an engine `NodeId` rather than the author key / `author_id` (§7 Screen Reader Support, actionable-key rule).

- a11y §7 Screen Reader Support (actionable-key rule, snapshot model) ↔ tests: the coverage and `actions`-replay tests read the same graph/snapshot the a11y-leg checks (`stand_accessibility_ids`) pin; a new test file joining the `a11y` leg's fourteen files or the `stand-repeat` list is §9 CI Integration's and test-plan §10's call.
- a11y §3 A11y Assertion Harness Contract ↔ obs: no a11y violation JSON schema is defined (§3 marked NOT YET MEASURED), so this chunk binds nothing there.

- On every stand task the coverage command's handler set names only graph nodes carrying an author key, agreeing with `unkeyed_actionable` returning nothing (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- The coverage output contains no control value, typed text or `NodeId` — ids, component and event names only (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- The existing `a11y` CI leg stays green with the chunk landed (per a11y-plan §9 CI Integration).

body:
Builds one handler-coverage command (v030-07): after a set of recorded kept checks has run on the stand through Check::from_bytes and Check::replay, it lists exactly the UI graph's handlers (graph node id and handler event name, as DioxusDocument::graph reads them) that none of those checks exercised.
Adds a record of which (element, event) handlers a run reached that holds on every app, registry or not, read beside the UI graph without changing its shape.
States the canvas limit in the acceptance: only DOM listeners on agent-visible nodes are counted, one per (node, event); handlers a canvas dispatches inside one listener are not, the count keyed on the graph's node id with its optional owner so 0.4.0 can extend it to virtual nodes.
Writes the owed replay test (CARRY cry-sxrivdk3): a session holding an actions step is recorded, kept, read back and replayed on a fresh session of the same app, the replay holding, and a differing actions answer naming the step and the differing key; v030-06 reads verified only once it passes.
The UI graph read DioxusDocument::graph, its UiGraph nodes, GraphNode.handlers and GraphHandler.event, and a node's optional owner: the coverage command reads them and keeps their shapes.

The graph-state registry (use_graph_state, DeclaredWrite, SignalRegistry and its dispatches record) and the bridge's handle_event setting the registry's dispatch only where a registry stands: the new exercised record must hold on apps with no registry.
The Dioxus DOM bridge's event path, DOM events reaching the vdom through data-dioxus-id, where the (element, event) handlers a run reached would be recorded.

Stable element ids (four tiers and the reserved owner form spelled by virtual_node_id): the coverage list is keyed on the graph's node id with its owner, never a NodeId, keeping the 0.4.0 virtual-node extension open.
The driver session: Session::run as the one path every call takes, validation first, nothing public running a Command not from validate; any coverage read or replay goes through it.

Kept checks and the recording: a session's answered calls kept as one owner-only replayable check, Check::from_bytes reading it back, Check::replay running every instance-verb step through Session::run; the owed test measures that a kept actions step replays and holds.

The actions verb and its answer (actionable_nodes, ActionableNode id, owner, keyed; owner ids, verb words, closed cause words and booleans on the wire): read by the replay test and compared key by key, its shape unchanged.

The driver's wire boundary: no NodeId crosses, nothing logs an id, a name or a value, every answer written by hand in the crate-private json module; the coverage answer carries only ids and component and event names the graph verb already carries, no control value or typed text.

The command and refusal schema stated once as static data, fourteen verbs and eight closed causes, carried by the v3 wire, the command line, the MCP server and the command and tool_call spans: a new verb would move it to fifteen and every pin that holds that count.
The escher-session command line and MCP tool listing over the six served stand tasks, exit codes 0, 1, 2, 3: where a new verb or argument lands.

The recording directory and kept-check medium: a path the launcher names by --record, owner-only, never named by a tool call; a call naming a check path on disk would be a new input class, a boundary widening that is the founder's.
A new carrier, exit, argument kind, result field or carrier content widens the driver session boundary and escalates at P4.

The headless stand (seven_guis::stand, its boots, Cells and the load page, pinned viewport and font): where the recorded checks run and the replay test records and replays on a fresh session of the same app.
The two committed stand checks under tests/blitz-tests/checks/ replayed by stand_replay, the one exception to owner-only kept checks.
A shot's PNG bytes differ across linux x86_64 and macOS aarch64: a kept check the replay test compares across OSes holds no screenshot step.
The capability statement docs/capabilities.md and README's count of driver commands an MCP client gets as tools, pinned by the capability-statement test: they move only if a verb is added.

The snapshot's clickable reading and the one actionable rule (focusable, an interactive role, or current listeners holding an event other than mounted): the coverage read stays consistent with what the graph counts as a handler, mounted excluded.
Telemetry and logging: escher-driver builds its spans by hand, ungated, installs no subscriber; no log or event carries the snapshot or the coverage list's names.

body_fields.convention: each integration test file covers one behavior and opens with a //! doc naming it; tests first assert the fixture produces the condition; scenarios run in both layout modes; unit tests in a cfg(test) mod tests at the file's end or a #[path] child file

cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings and rustdoc -D warnings over every library crate pass, each run through ci-leg.sh; expect_used and unwrap_used allowed only beside a justification
crate internals pub(crate) or pub(super); consuming builders with_ and without_
the per-crate coverage floor and the stand-repeat leg's zero-failure budget hold for new code and stand tests
body_fields.home: Infrastructure Patterns, CI/CD; occupied-resources file, res-ci-infrastructure

A new coverage verb is a schema change that every carrier must carry, and the founder rules on that boundary widening (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session).
- Under §Established Decisions → Driver session, no `NodeId` may cross a session. Only ids, names, closed flag words and booleans, and a UI graph's names cross. The coverage answer must key handlers on the graph's stable node id and its optional `owner`, and a new carrier or exit widens the boundary (per architecture §Established Decisions → Driver session).
- The UI graph (`DioxusDocument::graph`), the snapshot and the stable-id tiers, including the reserved `{owner}///{key}` virtual form, read the screen read-only and hold no `NodeId`. The coverage read must stay read-only and must not redefine the graph's shape (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).
- `serde_json` may only read MCP requests and kept checks. Any coverage answer must be hand-written in the crate-private `json` module, and no command's ending may write back anything the caller typed (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session).
- A kept check is a recording directory named only by the launcher's `--record <dir>`. It is never named by a tool call and is held owner-only `0700`. A verb that took a check path from a caller would be a new input class (per architecture §Occupied Resources → Filesystem).
- escher-driver depends on no app, emits no event, installs no subscriber and reads no env var. It builds its spans by hand, ungated, with no `#[instrument]` (per architecture §Established Decisions → Driver session; per architecture §Conventions → Feature gating).
- The snapshot and graph modules of dioxus-native-dom are gated by `accessibility`. `use_graph_state`/`SignalRegistry` stay ungated, and the bridge's `handle_event` sets the registry's dispatch only where a registry stands. Whether a per-(element, event) record of reached handlers holds on every app is research's question (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Config management; per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).

- `Check::from_bytes` then `Check::replay`, which runs each kept step again through `Session::run`. A masked `type` is kept as its stand-in and a shot is kept without its pixels. This is the path for the owed `actions`-step replay test (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session).
- `DioxusDocument::actionable_nodes` and `unkeyed_actionable` read one actionable rule (focusable, an interactive role, or current listeners holding an event other than `mounted`) and list results in snapshot pre-order. A handler-coverage reader should follow the same read-only, one-rule form (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).
- Integration tests use one behaviour per file and open with a `//!` doc. Stand checks share helpers through non-target modules under `tests/`. Tests first assert that the fixture produces the condition, and scenarios run in both layout modes (per architecture §Conventions → Tests).
- The headless stand (`seven_guis::stand`) boots the lean tasks, Cells and the load page offline in a pinned 800x600 Light viewport. It is the "on the stand" ground for both the coverage acceptance and the replay test (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Headless stand).

- No `NodeId` in any coverage answer, log or span. Nothing may log an id, a name or a value, and no log may carry the snapshot, its text or a diff beyond its three counts (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session; per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).
- No serialization crate may write an answer, and no tool call may take a recording or check path (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session; per architecture §Occupied Resources → Filesystem).
- A kept check compared byte for byte across OSes holds no `screenshot` step. The replay test's recorded session must not rely on one (per architecture §Existing Scopes).

- arch ↔ tests: a new verb moves the `VERBS` count pins named in scope §Premises (`.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py`, `docs/capabilities.md`, README's tool count). The README is read by the capability-statement pin (per architecture §Project Intent → Front page).
- arch ↔ obs: the driver's `command`/`tool_call` spans carry the schema, and escher-driver emits ungated spans with no subscriber (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Logging and timing).
- arch ↔ security: the session boundary (no `NodeId`, no caller-typed write-back, owner-only recording dir) governs what the coverage answer may carry (per architecture §Established Decisions → Driver session).

- (arch) The coverage answer keys each unexercised handler by the graph's stable node id (with optional `owner`) and event name. No `NodeId` crosses any carrier (per architecture §Established Decisions → Driver session).
- (arch) The coverage read mutates nothing. The graph, snapshot, stable-id grammar and `actions` shapes are unchanged (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).
- (arch) If a verb is added, it is stated once in the `'static` schema and carried consistently by the `v3` wire, the CLI, MCP and the spans, with the verb count pins updated together. Its answer is hand-written in the `json` module (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session).
- (arch) The owed test replays a kept `actions` step through `Check::from_bytes` and `Check::replay` on the stand in a one-behaviour integration test file opening with `//!` (per architecture §Conventions → Tests).

body:
Builds one handler-coverage command (v030-07): after a set of kept checks has been replayed on the stand, it lists exactly the UI graph's handlers (a graph node's id with its optional owner, and a handler's event name) that none of them exercised.
States the canvas limit in the acceptance: only DOM listeners on agent-visible nodes count, one per (node, event); handlers a canvas dispatches inside one listener are not counted, and 0.4.0 extends the count to virtual nodes.
Writes the owed replay test (CARRY cry-sxrivdk3): a recorded session holding an `actions` step, kept, read back through Check::from_bytes and replayed through Check::replay on a fresh session, holding; a differing `actions` answer names the step and the key. v030-06 reads verified once it passes.
Reads the UI graph, the snapshot, the stable-id grammar and the `actions` verb without changing their shapes; the coverage read is read-only over the screen.

The handler-coverage command itself: its answer lists (graph node id with optional owner, handler event name) pairs that no replayed kept check exercised, keyed on the graph's node id, never on a NodeId.

The UI graph as the `graph` verb carries it on the cli surface (cli-graph): GraphNode.handlers and GraphHandler.event, node ids with their optional owner; the command reads this shape and leaves it unchanged.
The `actions` verb's answer on the cli surface (cli-actions): the owed test keeps an `actions` step's answer whole and compares it on replay; a differing answer names the step and the differing key.

The pending unpaged graph and unpaged actions items (cli-unpaged-graph, cli-unpaged-actions): the coverage count reads the graph's handler set whole and the kept `actions` answer is compared whole, so any page bound on those answers reaches the count and the test.

The canvas limit: one DOM listener a canvas or custom widget holds (desktop-native-custom-widget) counts once per (node, event); the handlers it dispatches internally are not counted, and the acceptance says so, leaving 0.4.0's virtual-node extension open.

The record of which (element, event) handlers a run reached: the graph's confirmed flag and the signal registry's dispatched events hold only where an app registered a state, and the count must hold on every app, registry or not.
The check replay path: Check::from_bytes then Check::replay, each instance-verb step run through Session::run on a fresh session of the same app; the coverage command and the owed test both ride it.
The read-only boundary over the coverage answer: it runs no step of its own and carries no control value, typed text, page text beyond ids, component and event names, or NodeId.

The driver's verb count, if the command is a new verb: VERBS fourteen to fifteen and every pin holding that count (capability statement test, docs/capabilities.md, README tool count, schema_tests, cli_tests, stand_mcp_tools); the verb is named to the Cold-agent bar, not counted here.
The ledger states: v030-07 claimed by this chunk with its integration acceptance; v030-06 moves from implemented to verified only once the owed replay test passes.

body_fields.convention: every answer, refusal or session error a driver command emits on the command line or its mcp role is JSON only on stdout, one line per command or newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0, never colour or an ESC byte, the same piped or not, with the exit status carrying the class (0 accepted, 1 refused, 2 usage, 3 session error; an mcp Err ending exits 3)

Typography, font loading and the screenshot's fonts-unavailable refusal: the chunk takes no screenshot and measures no text.
Spacing: no layout value is set or read by the coverage count or the owed test.
Depth Strategy and its hit-testing clip rules: the coverage read dispatches no pointer and changes nothing on the screen.
Border Radius: no radius is drawn or measured.
Motion's into-view scroll rule and reduced-motion absence: the chunk adds no scrolling and no animation.
Iconography, cursors and favicons: the command has no visual output.
Desktop-native window, titlebar, devtools overlay and stack: the chunk builds no shell or window change.
Mobile-native surfaces (url bar, back button, capture, stack, tokens): the chunk touches no mobile build.

Web-spa surface and its WASM host canvas: that canvas is the page the native app renders into, not the in-app canvas whose internal handlers the acceptance leaves uncounted; no canvas renderer is built.
Cli tokens of the WPT runner and the paint_bench and screenshot example binaries (owo-colors terminal output): the coverage command is a driver surface, not those binaries.

body_fields.why: The coverage command must read the handlers from this `graph` answer, leave its shape unchanged, and carry no more than this line carries, never a value or typed text.
body_fields.quote: `escher-session graph` takes no argument, and an argument is refused `malformed` with nothing run; it answers the screen's whole UI graph as one uncoloured line of JSON `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}` on stdout, status `0`, the same answer on the session socket's `call` and in a kept check, and over the `mcp` role its tool result is the text block of that one line; the line carries ids, owner ids, component names, registered state names, handler event names, the closed flag words `undeclared` · `unconfirmed` and booleans only, never a value or typed text (packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:382-427; examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs:468-493; as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-07-ui-graph/report.md)

body_fields.why: The coverage count must read the graph's handler set whole, so it must hold against the graph's unpaged answer and its stated size on Cells.
body_fields.quote: The `graph` answer is unpaged, the whole screen in one line: Cells at boot answers 293,869 bytes — the stated limit «An unpaged graph» (docs/capabilities.md:270-273) · owner: residual `res-7cc5bi4k`, target next (as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-07-ui-graph/report.md)

body_fields.why: The owed replay test must keep an `actions` step's answer of exactly this shape in a check and compare it whole on replay, leaving the verb's shape unchanged.
body_fields.quote: `escher-session actions` takes no argument, and an argument is refused `malformed`; it answers one uncoloured line of JSON `{"nodes":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"keyed":…,"verbs":[{"verb":…,"cause":…}]}]}` on stdout, status `0`, the same answer on the session socket's `call`, over the `mcp` role and in a kept check; it lists every actionable node in snapshot pre-order — focusable, of an interactive role or holding a current listener for an event other than `mounted`, or owned by another node — each with the verb table's id-taking instance verbs and the cause each would be refused with, `owner` and `cause` left out when absent; the line carries ids, owner ids, the table's verb words, closed cause words and booleans only, never a value, typed text or `NodeId` (packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs:251-272; packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:429-452; examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs:495-516; as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here/report.md)

The `actions` answer reports whether each call would be accepted, not what it would do: a node's verbs are decided by the same `validate` and per-verb target check (`check_target`) that every id-taking verb meets before it acts, so a listed cause is the cause the call returns, and a node that resolves to no element reads `stale` (docs/capabilities.md:259-261; packages/escher-driver/src/actions.rs:40-102; packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:498-526; as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here/report.md)

body_fields.quote: The `actions` answer is unpaged, taking no argument and answering the whole screen in one line: Cells at boot answers 106,088 bytes for 678 nodes, within the 1,048,576-byte answer bound — the stated limit «An unpaged actions answer» beside «An unpaged graph» (docs/capabilities.md:274-276) · owner: residual `res-7cc5bi4k`, target next (as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here/report.md)

body_fields.why: Any record of reached handlers added in dioxus_document.rs must keep the render recorded into a mutation buffer and replayed under one borrow, with no `RefCell already borrowed` panic.
body_fields.quote: On every Dioxus document, the windowed `dioxus-native` launch and the headless stand alike, code the vdom runs during a render, a component body or a task it polls, can call `MountedData`'s `set_focus`, `get_client_rect`, `scroll_to`, `scroll`, `get_scroll_offset` and `get_scroll_size` with no `RefCell already borrowed` panic: the render is recorded into a mutation buffer with the document unborrowed, then replayed under one borrow; by construction such a call acts on the document as the previous render left it, so a node created in that same render is not yet in it and `set_focus_to` returns `false` for it (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:167-169; packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:315-317; packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_buffer.rs:97-140; as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render/report.md)

body: **cli-graph ↔ cli-unpaged-graph**: the coverage answer must list the (node id with optional owner, event) pairs read from the whole `graph` answer, carrying only ids, owner ids, component and handler event names (design-system/surface fct-gnekz77j), and it must hold over that answer unpaged at its measured Cells size (design-system/surface fct-bzczuomv).

**cli-actions ↔ cli-unpaged-actions**: the owed replay test must keep the `actions` answer whole in a check and find it equal on replay, its causes decided by `validate` and `check_target` (design-system/surface fct-rqe4xefm) (design-system/surface fct-cu455asz), the whole answer inside the 1,048,576-byte bound (design-system/surface fct-wvdzkcqu).

**cli-graph ↔ cli-actions**: a node holding a current listener for an event other than `mounted` is actionable (design-system/surface fct-rqe4xefm) and the graph names its handler events (design-system/surface fct-gnekz77j); the coverage count must key on the graph's node id with its optional owner, the same ids both answers carry, never a `NodeId`.

**desktop-native-stack ↔ cli-graph**: a record of which (element, event) handlers a run reached, if added in dioxus_document.rs, must keep the buffered render's single borrow (design-system/surface fct-zgbhkh7f) while the `graph` answer keeps its shape (design-system/surface fct-gnekz77j).

body:
Builds one handler-coverage command (v030-07): after a set of kept checks has been replayed on the stand through Check::from_bytes and Check::replay, it lists exactly the UI graph's handlers (a graph node id and a handler event name, as DioxusDocument::graph reads them) that none of those checks exercised.
Adds a record of which (element, event) handlers a run reached that holds on every app, registry or not, since the graph's confirmed flag and SignalRegistry::dispatches read only where an app registered a state.
States the canvas limit in the acceptance: only DOM listeners on agent-visible nodes are counted, one per (node, event); handlers a canvas dispatches inside one listener are not, the shape keyed on the graph node id with its optional owner, never on a NodeId.
Writes the owed replay test (CARRY cry-sxrivdk3): a recorded session holding an actions step, kept, read back and replayed on a fresh session, the replay holding, and a differing actions answer naming the step and the differing key; v030-06 reads verified only once it passes.
The coverage read is read-only: it runs no step of its own and carries no control value, typed text, page text beyond the graph verb's ids, component and event names, or NodeId.

The command span opened by execute for every call handed to Session::run: a coverage read or a replayed actions step runs under it, its eight fields closed words, bools and counts, never the screen text, an argument or an Outcome; escher-driver keeping its 2 info_span sites and emitting no event.

The tool_call span over MCP tools/call: if the coverage read becomes a verb, its tool word joins the verb table's closed words and its ending stays accepted, refused or error, two fields and no other.

How a new Outcome for the coverage answer is written: by Outcome::to_json alone as a command's answer, over MCP its JSON line, kept whole in a recorded check, never logged, fielded or printed with Debug, like Outcome::Graphed's ids, component names and handler event names.

The values the coverage answer may carry: graph node ids, the optional owner, component and handler event names only; no control value, typed text, page text or NodeId, as the graph answer already holds.

The recording module's kept check: each answered call's arguments, accepted, its answer's FNV-1a 64 digest and the answer itself written through the crate's json writer, a file at rest; the owed test's kept actions step lives there.

The replay module and Check::replay: no tracing site, env read or print, serde_json only to read; the replay test's failure message names the step and the differing key, never a captured answer or page text.
The recording directory's carve-out: owner-only 0700, refused when open to group or others, holding call content at rest, never a log or event line, uploaded by no CI leg.

dioxus-native-dom's handler-reach record (signal_registry dispatches, graph handlers, the bridge dispatch path): it adds no log site, span, field, log field or env read, the debug logs of mutation_writer untouched.

The sink's line format and allowlist scrub: any new span field or tool word passes the escher_ target rule, a content-named field printed only as [redacted], so no handler id or event name enters a field outside the closed set.
host_log and mcp_log: if a new verb lands, both read it at trace under both builds with 0 id, name and typed-text needles and one tool_call line per call.
The stand's headless boot in process installs no escher sink: the replay test and the coverage check replay checks in process on seven_guis::stand boots, so no sink line is produced by them.

The verb count pins if a fifteenth verb is added: VERBS fourteen to fifteen and the pins holding that count (test_capability_statement.py, docs/capabilities.md, README tool count, schema_tests.rs, cli_tests.rs, stand_mcp_tools), stand_mcp_tools' Recorder reading the tool_call and command spans.
The cold-agent pipe's server.log span counts by tool word and its counted verbs list: a new verb's place in that list is the Cold-agent bar entry's call, the pipe never printing server.log.
The canvas limit's statement: handlers a canvas dispatches internally are not counted, 0.4.0 extending the count to virtual nodes keyed on node id and owner, never redefining it.

body_fields.convention: each new test or check installs no subscriber, reads no env var and prints nothing, its readings going into assertions only, the silence census reading 0 over the file and any shared module it reads
a new reader of tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs, fixtures/mod.rs or common/mod.rs is recorded in that module's reader list and count
a new escher-driver module or function holds no tracing site, env read or print; the driver keeps its 2 info_span sites and the command span its eight fields
a new Outcome, result field or read type derives Debug only if nothing logs, fields or prints it; it is written once, by to_json, as a command's answer
a committed kept check or fixture holds no typed text, host path or secret
a new span field or MCP tool word is a closed word, bool or count, judged pair by pair by the sink's allowlist scrub

- obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage requires every call handed to `Session::run` to open exactly one INFO `command` span at target `escher_driver`, its eight fields closed words, bools and counts only; if the coverage read is a new verb, its `verb` field must be the verb table's own word, recorded alone (as for `graph` / `actions`), and no node id, event name, check path or argument may be fielded.
- obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage requires the MCP `tool_call` span to carry two fields only, `tool` (the verb table's word) and `ending` (`accepted` · `refused` · `error`); a fifteenth tool word is a new closed value of `tool`, and whether the code's verb table already holds such a word is research's question.
- obs-plan §6 Log Coverage requires escher-driver to emit no event and the `Session::actions` read to add no log site; a coverage read built beside it must likewise add no log site, print, env read or clock read, its answer written by `to_json` alone as a command's answer, never a log line.
- obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing & Compliance requires a graph or actions answer to carry ids, owner ids, closed words and booleans only, never a value, typed text, mask or `NodeId`, kept whole in a recorded check and never logged or fielded; a coverage answer (node id, optional `owner`, handler event name) falls under the same rule and is a boundary widening the founder ratifies.
- obs-plan §3 Observability Harness Contract requires the stand checks and the session library to install no subscriber, read no env var and print nothing (the `stand_act_spans` children and `stand_mcp_tools` recorder aside); the owed `actions`-replay test and any coverage check must join that silence.
- obs-plan §9 CI Integration requires a recording directory to stay local (`0700`, never a log or event line) and committed kept checks to hold no typed text, host path or secret; a check kept by the owed test, if committed, must meet that.

- `stand_act_spans` per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage: one call per layout mode for each verb, its `command` line recording `verb` alone — the pattern a new coverage verb extends.
- `stand_mcp_tools` per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage: an in-process `Recorder` asserting a `tool_call` parents a `command` span recording its verb alone (as its `actions` test does).
- `host_log` / `mcp_log` per obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing & Compliance: one call of the verb at `trace` under both builds, reading 0 id, name and verb-specific needles (`actions_needles` in `examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs`) — the pattern for a coverage verb's needle check.
- `stand_session_recording` / `stand_replay` per obs-plan §3 Observability Harness Contract (absence · logs detail): replay through `Check::replay` with failure messages holding the mode, the file and a step index alone, no subscriber, env read or print — the shape for the owed `actions`-replay test's failure naming the step and differing key.

- No logging, fielding or `Debug`-printing of an `Outcome` (a graph, actions or coverage answer) or of a kept check's contents, per obs-plan §3 Observability Harness Contract (session library: `Outcome` written in one place, by `Outcome::to_json`).
- No caller-typed verb text, check path or handler event name recorded on a span, per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage.

- obs ↔ tests: a new verb moves `stand_act_spans`, `stand_mcp_tools`, `host_log` and `mcp_log` (span and needle counts) and the verb-count pins the scope lists; the owed replay test joins the silence census over `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs` readers (obs-plan §3 Observability Harness Contract; test-plan §3).
- obs ↔ security: a coverage answer's content (ids, event names) is a boundary widening, the §8 crossing the founder ratifies (obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing & Compliance).
- obs ↔ cold-agent pipe: a fifteenth tool word reaches the pipe's verb list and `span_counts` only if it is made a counted verb — «Cold-agent bar»'s call (obs-plan §6 Log Coverage).

- (obs) If a coverage verb is added: `stand_act_spans` shows one `command` line per layout mode with `verb` that word alone, and `stand_mcp_tools` one `tool_call` parenting it (per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage).

body:
Builds one handler-coverage command (v030-07): after a set of kept checks (check-{n}.json, read by Check::from_bytes and run by Check::replay) has run on the stand, it lists exactly the UI graph's handlers (graph node id with its optional owner, handler event name) that none of those checks exercised.
Adds a record of which (element, event) handlers a run reached that holds on every Dioxus app, registry or not, read beside the bridge's event dispatch and the SignalRegistry; the coverage read is read-only, runs no step and carries no NodeId, control value or typed text.
States the canvas limit in the acceptance: only DOM listeners on agent-visible nodes count, one per (node, event); handlers a canvas dispatches inside one listener are not counted, and 0.4.0 extends the count to virtual nodes.
Writes the owed replay test (CARRY cry-sxrivdk3) for v030-06: a session holding an actions step is recorded, kept, read back through Check::from_bytes and replayed on a fresh session, the kept actions answer matching, and a differing answer naming the step and the differing key.
How checks reach the command (in-process replay or a new verb naming checks) is a P4 fork; a new verb would move the driver's verb table from fourteen to fifteen and every pin of that count.

The driver command schema: validate checks every call against a closed table of fourteen verbs and seven bounded argument kinds; a new coverage verb or argument kind must join that table, pass validate, and keep the fixed refusal order, and nothing public may run a Command that did not come from validate.

The widening rule over the session socket and MCP carriers: a new field of a closed value set inside a ratified carrier is no widening, while a new verb, an argument naming a path on disk, an open value set or a new carrier is a boundary widening that escalates to the founder.

What the socket and MCP replies may carry: ids, names, a UI graph's ids, component, state and handler event names, closed words and booleans, never an attribute's text and no NodeId; a coverage answer of graph node ids, owner ids and handler event names must stay inside that set.
The stable element id grammar: the coverage list keys on the graph's stable id (with its optional owner), never a NodeId kept between calls, and the grammar keeps its shape.

The recorded check reader Check::from_bytes: a kept check's bytes are untrusted, read strictly under byte and record bounds with closed keys, anything else refused malformed holding nothing of the file, no panic path; every replayed step still passes validate inside Session::run, which the owed actions replay test exercises.

Kept check files and the recording directory: created 0600 in a 0700 directory, a group- or other-open directory refused, never replaced, no verb or result field naming the directory, nothing of it logged; the replay test's kept check lives so.
Committed checks: only counter-cli.json and counter-mcp.json are committed; a check the new tests record (an actions step included) stays owner-only and is never committed.

Masking of control values: a password's or file input's value reads as MASKED_VALUE in every carrier and kept check; the actions answer the replay compares and the coverage answer carry no control value or typed text.

The Dioxus bridge dispatch: the event dispatch sets a registered SignalRegistry's dispatch around runtime.handle_event and clears it after, inert where no state is registered; a new reached-handler record beside it must take dioxus-core types alone, hold no state value, and have no log site, print, env read or unwrap on app input.

The UI graph and the actions verb as carried on the socket and MCP (graph node ids, component, state and handler event names, actions answers' ids, owner ids, verb words, cause words, keyed booleans): the chunk reads them and must not change their shapes.

Typed refusals and session errors: a refusal of a coverage call is one of the closed causes with a fixed name, meaning and remedy, no String field, nothing a call supplied; MCP protocol errors fixed codes with no data.

The command span and escher's log sink: one command span per call holds fixed words, bools and counts only, never a call's content or the screen; a coverage count logged under an escher_ target passes the escher_telemetry allowlist, the crate installing no subscriber and reading no env var.

The escher-session command line: a new verb is read by the closed command_line reader, validated before the session address is asked for, with the four fixed exit statuses and no ending echoing what the caller typed.
The MCP server role: a new tool's arguments are typed then validated, results bounded, no print, unwrap, expect or panic outside tests, the request id the one echoed value.

serde_json as the reader of a kept check's bytes and of the driver's answer line the replay compares (no preserve_order), writing nothing; the actions answer equality the test asserts reads through it.

The driver's env reads: the escher-driver library and escher-session read no env var beyond RUST_LOG; the new tests reach their directories only through CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR, CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR or the workspace target/tmp.

body_fields.convention: each new test that records or keeps a check writes it 0600 in a 0700 directory under the test target directory, never commits it, and reads it back only through Check::from_bytes
each new test reaches its directories only through compile-time CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR or CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, never a new runtime env read
each new log line or span field under an escher_ target holds fixed words, bools and counts only and passes the escher_telemetry allowlist
each new or changed CI cargo command passes --locked, and every ci.yml uses: stays pinned to a commit SHA

body: **2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — built `validate`: a closed table of verbs and bounded argument kinds, a typed `Command` or a `Refusal` in fixed order, no `unwrap`/`expect`/panic/index on call input, no clock, no `Session`; `Refusal` a closed cause set with no `String` field; and no verb has an argument or result field of a wait. A coverage verb, if added, joins this table under these rules, and any coverage or replay-mismatch refusal must stay a closed cause holding nothing of the call or the file; rule: the first surface reaching `validate` from outside is its own crossing question.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `Session::run` calls `validate` first and nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from it. The owed replay test and any coverage read rest on this: every replayed `actions` step goes through `Session::run`.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** (what the driver logs) — one `command` span per call with fixed-word, bool and count fields only, never an argument, `Fault` or screen text; of a refusal only its cause's fixed name reaches a log. Binds any coverage field on the span to fixed words, bools and counts.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — `escher_telemetry::init`'s three-outcome sink: engine targets print safe fields, `escher_` targets print with the content-named fields redacted, any other target dropped; trap: a "nothing in the logs" check must run against a host that installs the sink (`host_log`). Anything the coverage read or reached-handler record emits passes this allowlist and is measured by `host_log`/`mcp_log`.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** (the session socket: threat vector, access) — the socket's access is the filesystem's alone: state directory `0700` (a group- or other-open one refused `StateDirNotPrivate`), socket `0600`, no handshake, token or peer check. A coverage call on the socket adds no auth and loosens no mode.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** — the socket carries calls and answers (a widening ratified by the founder), and the command line became an external input surface read by the closed `command_line` reader, the call checked by `validate`/`validate_session` before the session address is asked for, four fixed exit statuses, no ending writing back anything typed; standing rule: every later surface's input passes `validate` first and a `Refusal`, usage line or session error holds nothing caller-supplied. A coverage verb's CLI arm and any check-naming argument fall under this.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** (the closed-field rule) — the founder's widening rule: a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a widening; authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is. This is the test the coverage answer's fields and any new verb/argument are read against at P4.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — the MCP stdio crossing ratified: typed tool arguments then `validate`, fixed protocol errors with no `data`, bounded request lines and results, no auth, binds nothing; `serde_json` admitted as a reader only, no `preserve_order`. A coverage tool joins `tools/list` under these bounds, and the replay test's answer comparison reads through this `serde_json`.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — `help` admitted; the program's own fixed `'static` table text crossing out is inside the carriers, while text from a page, a call or a screen, a new carrier or exit still widens (a playbook rule). A coverage verb's help and result-field descriptions are fixed table text under this rule; `SESSION_ERRORS` table form.

**2026-10-19-session-recording** (kept check at rest, its directory, its reader, `--record`) — the recording directory row (`0700`, `check-{n}.json` `0600` `create_new`, bounds 400 records / 1,048,576 bytes, ending `recording-failed`, never named by any tool call or field, never logged) and the strict `Check::from_bytes` reader (closed keys, anything else `malformed` holding nothing, no panic path, each `Call` through `call_of` so a replayed step passes `validate` again); a masked `type` kept as `MASKED_STAND_IN`. The owed replay test records into and reads back through exactly these; a path that feeds checks to a coverage command is this reader's input class.

**2026-10-19-session-recording** (wire v3, session errors, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`) — wire `v3` with `recording-failed`, `SESSION_ERRORS` 15, `call_of` in `command.rs`, `serde_json` also reading kept-check bytes, and `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` read at build time by escher-driver's unit tests for the workspace `target/tmp`. Precedent for where a test-recorded check may live and which env reads a new test may rely on without a registration.

**2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay** — each kept answer kept whole at rest; `Check::replay` runs each kept step through `Session::run` alone, nothing on another app's session, `Replay`/`Change` holding bools, counts and closed words only; only `counter-cli.json` and `counter-mcp.json` committed (no typed text, host path, name, secret or `screenshot` step), every other check owner-only and never committed; `serde_json` reads the answer line the replay compares. Binds the owed `actions` replay test (not committing its check) and the differing-key report's form.

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** (the gated part: the `lint` verb on every carrier) — precedent for adding a no-argument read verb onto every ratified carrier: founder-ratified widening, an argument refused `malformed`, one result field written by `to_json` alone, never fielded on the span, kept in a recording with its answer whole, and the verb counts moved in the cold-agent check, recording rows, MCP `tools/list` and logging needles.

**2026-10-14-quality-gates** — `TMPDIR`, read by escher-driver's client unit test through `std::env::temp_dir()`, registered test-only (operator's answer: no crossing); the library reads none beyond `RUST_LOG`. A replay test placing its owner-only recording under a temp dir rides this precedent; a new env read elsewhere must be registered.

**2026-10-24-stand-requirement-sweep** — seven_guis `host_log` became the standing check of a recording session's clients at `RUST_LOG=trace` (`start crud --record`, 0 id, name, sentinel, recording-path and recorded needles, both builds). Where a coverage verb or a check-reading path is added, this is the needle check that must hold.

- security-plan §Input Validation (driver session socket, the widening rule) requires that any new verb, argument kind, result field, carrier or exit for handler coverage be treated as a boundary widening (founder-ratified), while a new closed-value field inside an already ratified carrier is not; a verb or argument naming a check path on disk would be a new input class on every carrier (the scope's P4 fork).
- security-plan §Input Validation (driver command schema) requires a new verb, if added, to enter the closed `'static` verb table and pass `validate`/`validate_session` on socket, CLI and MCP alike, with no `unwrap`/`expect`/panic on call-supplied input, no clock read, no `NodeId` kept between calls, and its `command` span holding fixed words, bools and counts only.
- security-plan §Threat Model Summary (local IPC and local stdio vectors) requires the coverage answer to carry only what the UI graph already carries — ids, component and handler event names, closed flag words and booleans, owner ids — and no `NodeId`, typed text, control value or attribute text; whether a coverage answer stays within that set is research's question.
- security-plan §Input Validation (recorded check, `Check::from_bytes`) requires a kept check's bytes to be read as untrusted: strict, bounded in bytes and records, closed keys, anything else refused `malformed` holding nothing of the file, no panic path, and every replayed step re-passing `validate` inside `Session::run` — this binds the owed `actions`-step replay test and any path that feeds checks to the coverage command.
- security-plan §Data Protection (files, kept and committed checks) requires a test-recorded check to live in a `0700` directory as `0600` files, never logged; only the two named stand-Counter checks are committed, so a new kept check holding an `actions` step is not committed unless it is ratified under the same rule (no typed text, host path, name, secret or `screenshot` step).
- security-plan §Error Handling (escher-driver `Refusal`) requires any refusal the coverage command or the replay mismatch path produces to be a typed value from the closed cause set with no `String` field, so it cannot echo call- or file-supplied content; whether a differing-`actions` replay report naming "the step and the differing key" fits this form is research's question.
- security-plan §Input Validation (Dioxus bridge) requires the in-process signal registry to take dioxus-core types alone with no log site, print, env read or `unwrap` on app input; a new per-(element, event) dispatch record holding on every app must keep that, adding no outside input class.

- Closed schema gate: every call passes `validate` to a typed `Command` or `Refusal`, the first failure in fixed order (per security-plan §Input Validation, driver command schema).
- Strict kept-check reader `Check::from_bytes` followed by `Check::replay` running each step through `Session::run` (per security-plan §Input Validation, recorded check).
- Recording directory discipline under `--record`/`Session::recording_into`: `0700` directory, `0600` files never replaced, nothing of the path logged (per security-plan §Input Validation, driver recording directory).
- Telemetry sink allowlist: `escher_` targets keep all but the content-named fields; anything new emitted by the coverage read goes through `escher_telemetry::init`'s allowlist (per security-plan §Logging & Monitoring).

- No `NodeId`, typed text, control value or attribute text in a coverage answer, a span or a log line (per security-plan §Input Validation, driver session socket).
- No `String` field in a refusal or error carrying caller- or check-supplied content back out (per security-plan §Error Handling).
- No path-on-disk argument, env read or cwd-relative default introduced to locate checks without an explicit founder-ratified widening (per security-plan §Input Validation, driver session state directory and the widening rule).

- security ↔ tests: the owed `actions` replay test records into an owner-only directory and must not commit its kept check (security-plan §Data Protection); verb-count pins (`schema_tests.rs`, `cli_tests.rs`, `stand_mcp_tools`, `test_capability_statement.py`) move with any new verb.
- security ↔ obs: any new `command` span or event fields stay fixed words, bools and counts under the escher-telemetry allowlist (security-plan §Logging & Monitoring).
- security ↔ arch: a new verb or result field is a boundary widening the founder ratifies at P4 (security-plan §Input Validation, the widening rule); the cold-agent verb list is «Cold-agent bar»'s.

- (security) If a coverage verb is added, a call with an unknown argument, an `id` naming no element, or an oversized line is refused with nothing run, on socket, CLI and MCP (per security-plan §Input Validation).
- (security) The coverage answer, by test, holds only graph ids, owner ids and handler event names plus closed words, booleans and counts — no `NodeId`, typed text or masked value (per security-plan §Threat Model Summary).
- (security) A malformed or tampered kept check fed to the replay/coverage path is refused `malformed`, holding nothing of the file, with no panic (per security-plan §Input Validation).
- (security) No new kept check is committed to the tree beyond `counter-cli.json` and `counter-mcp.json` unless ratified under the committed-checks rule (per security-plan §Data Protection).

body:
Builds one handler-coverage command (v030-07): after a set of recorded checks (kept checks read through Check::from_bytes and run through Check::replay) has run on the seven_guis stand, it lists exactly the UI graph's handlers (a graph node id and a handler event name, as DioxusDocument::graph reads them) that none of those checks exercised.
States in the acceptance that handlers a canvas dispatches internally, inside one listener, are not counted; 0.4.0 extends the count to virtual nodes, so the command stays keyed on the graph node id with its optional owner, never on a NodeId.
Adds a record of which (element, event) handlers a run reached that holds on every app, registry or not, read with the signal registry, the bridge's dispatch record and the graph reader in dioxus-native-dom.
Writes the owed replay test (CARRY cry-sxrivdk3): a recorded session holding an actions step, kept as a check, read back and replayed on a fresh session of the same app, the replay holding, and a differing actions answer naming the step and the differing key; v030-06 reads verified only once it passes.
The coverage read is read-only over the screen: no step of its own, no control value, typed text or NodeId, and the UI graph, snapshot, stable-id grammar and actions verb keep their shapes.

The UI graph reader DioxusDocument::graph, its GraphNode.handlers and GraphHandler.event, the graph verb and the stand_graph check that reads it on every served screen in both layout modes, with the GRAPH_DRIVES table and Drive enum in tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs.

The bridge's dispatch record, SignalRegistry::dispatches() and the graph's confirmed flag, with the dioxus-native-dom unit tests over the bridge, the signal registry and the graph reader, the bridge_tests child module and its cfg(test) shim dispatch_to_vdom; the new exercised record must hold on an app that registers no state.

Recorded-check replay: kept checks committed under tests/blitz-tests/checks, run as cargo test targets through Check::replay, red at the first step whose acceptance or kept answer differs, and kept fresh byte-for-byte against what escher-session records; the stand_replay check and seven_guis recording target that embed them.

The owed actions-step replay test: recording a session with an actions step (stand_session_recording, session_common's kept and shot_prefix readers), reading it back through Check::from_bytes, replaying on a fresh session, and asserting a differing actions answer names the step and the key.

The actions verb and its stand_actions check (each served screen's actionable nodes, every listed cause what the call returns, both layout modes, changing nothing), whose answer the replay test keeps and compares.

Session to held instance integration: an escher_driver Session booted through seven_guis::stand, calls run through Session::run returning after settle, both layout modes, and the session_common builders (hold, act, graphed, refused) a coverage check would use.

The read-only boundary of the coverage read: it changes nothing on screen and carries no control value, typed text, page text beyond ids, component and event names, or NodeId, checked as the graph and actions verbs are (snapshot unchanged before and after).

The canvas limit and the reserved virtual form of the stable element id: the count is DOM listeners on agent-visible nodes, one per (node, event); canvas-internal handlers are not counted and no virtual node is produced.

If the command is a new driver verb: VERBS fourteen to fifteen and every pin of that count — test_capability_statement.py over docs/capabilities.md and README's tool count, schema_tests.rs, cli_tests.rs, stand_mcp_tools — plus the verb's word in the closed tool_call and command span sets; the cold-agent pipe's verb list and isolated tool set are named to «Cold-agent bar», not counted here.

The driver's log discipline: one escher_driver command line per call with fixed words and counts only, and host_log and mcp_log reading 0 id, name and graph needles at RUST_LOG=trace under both builds for any new verb.
The escher-driver unit tests of the verb schema, command validation, JSON forms, command line, MCP, recording and replay, which a new verb, argument kind or result field reaches.
Per-crate coverage floors in the coverage leg: packages/escher-driver 97 % and packages/dioxus-native-dom 83 %, which the new code and its tests must keep.
The stand-repeat leg's zero-failure flakiness budget (stand_*.rs files, the seventeen named targets, seven_guis process checks, three rounds, no retry), which the new checks join.
The agent-run contract's run stand count (newest 244 · 0 · 7 over 52 files): a new stand_ file is picked up with no script change and the recount is stated in the report.

v030-07's acceptance by integration method (after a set of recorded checks has run on the stand, one command lists exactly the unexercised handlers), and v030-06 flipping from implemented to verified on the owed test's pass.

relevant

- The owed replay test (CARRY cry-sxrivdk3) is the open item test-plan §5 Integration Test Strategy names as owed ("A kept actions step's replay, owed", fct-kzdrls5d); it should be an integration check in tests/blitz-tests/tests/ that measures what is now "by construction, unmeasured". Whether `Check::replay` already holds on a kept `actions` step is what the test has to show, not something to assume (per test-plan §5 Integration Test Strategy).
- Recorded-check replay is required to run as an ordinary `cargo test` target through `Check::from_bytes` then `Check::replay`, every step re-validated through `Session::run`, red at the first step whose acceptance or kept answer (compared as a JSON value) differs (per test-plan §2 Test Strategy, Recorded-check replay).
- The replay contract under test is `Check::replay(&mut Session) -> Replay` with `Replay { holds, another_app, ran, change }` and `Change { step, accepted_then, accepted_now, keys, refused }`, `keys` being the verb's result fields that differ, in table order. The "differing actions answer names the step and the key" assertion reads `Change.step` and `Change.keys`. Recording is unix-only (`Session::recording_into` returns `Unsupported` elsewhere), so the record-then-replay test is `cfg(unix)`-gated or reads a committed check (per test-plan §3 `session-start`, contract doc:test-plan/contracts/session-lifecycle).
- Session checks hold a session through `tests/session_common/mod.rs` (`hold`, `act`, the call builders `graph()` and so on) or through `tests/fixtures/mod.rs` (`boot`, `hold`), in both layout modes (`incremental` true and false). A new builder or reader goes into the shared module and is not redefined in each file (per test-plan §3 Test Harness Contract, blitz-tests (session checks) and blitz-tests (fixtures)).
- The handler-coverage read is required to change nothing on the screen, like `graph` and `actions` (`stand_graph`, `stand_actions`). Its check asserts that the snapshot and focus are unchanged across the call, in both layout modes (per test-plan §5 Integration Test Strategy, Session ↔ held instance).
- The stand checks have a zero-failure flakiness budget: a new `stand_*.rs` file enters `stand-repeat` (three rounds, no retry) through its glob, and it has to stay green there (per test-plan §10 Quality Gates & Coverage Targets, Flakiness budget).
- Coverage floors bind per crate: `packages/escher-driver` 97 %, `packages/dioxus-native-dom` 83 %. Any code added to either crate (a dispatch record or a coverage reader) must keep the crate at or above its floor in the `coverage` leg (per test-plan §10 Quality Gates & Coverage Targets, Coverage floors).

- Stand checks are picked up by the `stand_` prefix: `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run stand` selects every `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs` file with no script change, and `run {name}` runs one file. The newest reading is passed 244 · failed 0 · ignored 7 over 52 files (per test-plan §3 Test Harness Contract, `run {selection}` and Proof, the newest reading).
- `session_common` already has the readers `graphed(session, call)` (a `UiGraph`), `refused`, `refused_unchanged` and `act`. A coverage check reads the graph's `GraphNode.handlers` / `GraphHandler.event` through these readers. `GRAPH_DRIVES` in `tests/common/mod.rs` lists each stand task's drives (seven rows), which makes it a ready-made "set of checks that exercised" fixture (per test-plan §3 Test Harness Contract, blitz-tests (stand checks) and blitz-tests (session checks)).
- Committed checks live under `tests/blitz-tests/checks/` (counter-cli.json, counter-mcp.json), are embedded as bytes by `stand_replay`, and are kept fresh by seven_guis `recording`'s byte-for-byte comparison through `record_checks.sh`. A committed check with an `actions` step would follow this path and hold no typed text, host path, secret or `screenshot` step (per test-plan §7 Test Data & Fixtures, tests/blitz-tests/checks).
- Bridge-level unit tests in dioxus-native-dom sit in the `bridge_tests` child module (`dioxus_document_tests.rs`) and use the `cfg(test)` shim `DioxusDocument::dispatch_to_vdom`. A record of dispatched (element, event) pairs would be pinned there, adding no `pub` or constructor beyond what the test needs (per test-plan §3 Test Harness Contract, Crate-local test helpers, dioxus-native-dom).

- No sleep and no wall-clock read in session checks except where wall time is the subject. A replay or coverage check moves time only through the driver's `advance` (per test-plan §5 Integration Test Strategy, Wall time in the session checks).
- Do not add a test framework and do not give stand checks a skip path: the headless-stand checks assert unconditionally under the bundled DejaVu Sans (per test-plan §2 Test Strategy, Font-dependent tests and Command-line checks and shell flows).
- A check compared byte for byte across OSes holds no shot. A committed check that carries an `actions` step must not carry a `screenshot` step (per test-plan §2 Test Strategy, Pixel tests).

- tests ↔ obs: if the command becomes a new driver verb, it joins the closed `verb` / `tool` sets of the `command` and `tool_call` spans with no span field added. `host_log` / `mcp_log` must then read 0 id, name and graph needles at `trace` under both builds, as they do for `graph` and `actions` (per test-plan §3 Test Harness Contract, Stand log format; obs-plan §4).
- tests ↔ capability statement / cold agent: a fifteenth verb moves the pins of `test_capability_statement.py` (docs/capabilities.md, README tool count) and the cold-agent pipe's fourteen-verb `valid_step` and `isolated` checks. Per scope, the cold-agent verb count belongs to «Cold-agent bar» (per test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy, Capability statement; test-plan §3 Test Harness Contract, The server and the check's judge).
